sentences.text: Last, how does Rule nineteen hand back to the other rules?
The moment two vessels actually sight one another, the rules for vessels in sight take over: Rules eleven through eighteen.
A stand-on vessel and a give-way vessel exist again.
So picture a boat breaking out of the fog two hundred yards off your starboard bow.
You’re in a crossing situation, and you’re the give-way vessel.
But radar alone never makes you in sight.
And Rule seven’s warning applies with full force here: no assumptions on scanty radar information.
The fog signals themselves are in Rule thirty-five, and we’ll learn them in lesson fourteen.
In or near fog, and not in sight, nobody stands on.
Radar target ahead: don’t turn to port.
Fog signal forward of the beam: slow to bare steerageway, and stop if you must.
Next time, we start the lights, beginning with the ones on your own boat.
